requirements.text: A status attribute is mandatory in all documents with values of: original, copy, revision, cancellation.

The messages are specified for implementation as electronic documents, exchanged between Buyer and Seller, marked-up using eXtensible Markup Language (XML) and validated using XML schema, in compliance with the e-Government Interoperability Framework (e-GIF).
The Document UUID must be a computer generated unique identifier for the Document, guaranteed to be unique.
The Document ID must be the Document identifier within the sender's system.
The Document Date must be the date or date/time assigned to the Document by the sender using format CCYYMMDDhhmmss.
The Document Status must be one of original, copy, revision, or cancellation.
The Test Status must be a boolean indicating if the document is for test purposes only.
The Sender Software Manufacturer must be identified by a Universal Resource Identifier (URI).
The Sender Software Product must be the software manufacturer's name for the product.
The Sender Software Version must be the software manufacturer's product version.
The Schema Version must be the version of the XML schema with which the document complies.
The Line UUID must be a unique instance identifier for the Line.
The Line Number must be a positive integer starting with 1, with a maximum value of 9999.
The Line Status must be one of original, revision, or deletion.
The Line Quantity must be the quantity of goods or services on a Line.
The Amount Ex VAT must be the monetary amount excluding VAT on the Line.
The Item Name must be the name of the Item in a form mutually understood by both Buyer and Seller, limited to 70 characters.
The Unit of Measure must be a code describing the quantity in which goods and services are priced and ordered using a sub-set of UN recommendation No 20.
The Unit Price must include a currency code expressed using ISO 4217 3-character codes.
The Commodity Class must be the commodity class for the Item using UNSPSC or another classification agreed with OGC.
The Extended Item ID must be any part number of the Item other than the Seller Item ID or GTIN.
The Extended Item ID Source must specify the origin of the Extended Item ID.
The Aspect Name must be the name of the aspect.
The Aspect Value must be the value of the aspect.
The Aspect Value Unit must be the value unit associated with the aspect value.
Define the mandatory cryptographic algorithms, key lengths, and certificate validation requirements for the Digital Signature element to ensure non-repudiation and integrity.
Mandate that production systems must explicitly reject any document where Test Status is true, and define a secure mechanism for environment isolation.
Require that all documents containing sensitive financial identifiers (e.g., Account Number, Card Number, CVV) must be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and protected at rest.
The specification shall define a standard error response message format and mandatory error codes for handling schema validation failures and sequence errors.
The specification shall require that all exchanged documents be stored by both sender and receiver for a minimum of 7 years to ensure auditability and compliance with fiscal regulations.

The specification shall mandate the use of XML-DSig with SHA-256 or higher, and define that documents with invalid signatures must be rejected with a specific 'Security Validation Failure' error code.
The specification shall limit the number of lines per document to 9999 and the total XML payload size to 10MB to ensure predictable processing performance.
Define maximum allowed XML message size (e.g., 5MB) and target processing latency for document validation and parsing to ensure system responsiveness.
Include a section on 'Scalability Requirements' specifying the expected peak transactions per second (TPS) and total daily volume to guide implementers on infrastructure sizing.
